items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: I was at a clinic by Joe Lovano years ago and he talked about how horn players are so used to having what they play when they improvise be determined by how much air they have in their lungs.

ctx.x: One more comment about that gig followed with “Moment’s Notice” and it was bright. And I was wondering, in a tune like that, at that tempo with chord changes flying by are you thinking of the chord changes as you’re playing to guide your note choices? Or is it something else? © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Yeah I mean it’s that. I mean you have to — to be able to speak on a tune it’s very important to know the inner-workings of it I’d say. But I say ultimately you want to get to the point where you can play over the tune but you don’t have to think about what those chord changes are, you just know what the phrase is. And you can like speak over how the melody that — because I’m a single note instrument so I can only play one note at a time. So it’s like I have to know how what melody I’m playing relates to the…
Do you find that there’s been occasions where you play less, a bit less, because you’re working with such wonderful — a wonderful rhythm section?
